job.style: a conversation between a teacher and two students

passage: In class, Ms. Sharma discussed the nature of democracy with Rohan and Meera. Rohan asked, 'Is a country a democracy just because it has a parliament?' Ms. Sharma shook her head, 'Not necessarily. A parliament must be elected through free and fair competition where the ruling party has a real chance of losing.' Meera then asked, 'Does democracy mean the majority can do whatever they want?' Ms. Sharma replied, 'No, that is a common mistake. A true democracy must protect the rights of the minority, even if the majority disagrees. The government is bound by the rule of law and the constitution.' Rohan pondered this and said, 'So, if everyone is allowed to vote, the election is automatically fair?' Ms. Sharma clarified, 'Universal adult franchise is necessary, but not sufficient. For an election to be truly free and fair, there must be a level playing field where opposition parties can campaign without fear or government interference. Democracy is not just about the act of voting or the existence of a legislative body; it is about the limitations placed on power and the protection of individual dignity.'

items.evidence: A parliament must be elected through free and fair competition where the ruling party has a real chance of losing.
items.q: Country X has an elected parliament, but its ruling party can never lose. What is missing for democracy?
options: A real chance for rulers to be voted out
A longer gap between one election and the next
Power for the majority to do anything it wants
People voting directly on every single law
items.explain: A parliament counts only if the ruling party has a real chance of losing in fair competition.

wrong.why: thinks fewer elections let leaders rule properly
thinks democracy means unlimited majority power
thinks people must decide everything directly

items.evidence: A true democracy must protect the rights of the minority, even if the majority disagrees.
items.q: Most people in a country vote to ban a small group's festival. What should a true democracy do?
options: Protect the group's rights despite the vote
Ban the festival because most people want it
Let army officers settle the matter instead
Ban it, since all adults could vote
items.explain: A true democracy protects minority rights even when the majority disagrees.

wrong.why: thinks the majority can do whatever it wants
thinks unelected officials can hold final power
thinks a universal vote makes any result fair

items.evidence: The government is bound by the rule of law and the constitution.
items.q: A prime minister wants to ignore the constitution. What does the passage say about this leader?
options: The leader must follow it like everyone else
The leader stands above it while in office
The leader may ignore it if most agree
The leader may ignore it if very skilled
items.explain: The government is bound by the rule of law and constitution, so no leader is above it.

wrong.why: thinks top leaders are above the law
thinks majority support overrides the constitution
thinks skill gives a ruler final power

items.evidence: For an election to be truly free and fair, there must be a level playing field where opposition parties can campaign without fear or government interference.
items.q: Every adult can vote, but police break up opposition rallies. Why is this election still unfair?
options: Rival parties cannot campaign safely and freely
Rival parties compete, which only causes quarrels
Voters did not decide every law directly
Voting is not needed in a fair election
items.explain: Fair elections need a level playing field where opposition parties campaign without fear or interference.

wrong.why: thinks competition for power is the problem
thinks democracy means direct decisions on everything
